item.title: ACLU claims Ball State’s campus rules violate First Amendment rights
item.description: The ACLU of Indiana filed two federal lawsuits against Ball State University over a new rule that prohibits protests and demonstrations within fifty feet of most campus buildings, and the use of campus rules to punish students who expressed concern about Ball State's financial ties to Israel.

item.title: Professional Bull Riders event returns to Gainbridge Fieldhouse
item.description: Forty of the world's top Professional Bull Riders athletes will compete at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis on March 21-22, with tickets starting at $33 for the Saturday night event.

item.title: Israeli consul general to US Midwest advises Americans to leave Middle East
item.description: Israel's consul general to the U.S. Midwest is working with the U.S. embassy to help Americans in Israel get home. The State Department has urged Americans to leave the Middle East due to serious safety risks amid the Iran war.

item.title: Explosions sound in the Iranian capital as war with US and Israel enters a fifth day
item.description: Israel and the US have launched a joint military campaign against Iran, resulting in hundreds of deaths and escalating tensions in the Middle East, while Iran has retaliated by attacking US embassies and energy facilities in the region.

item.title: Georgia father found guilty of second-degree murder in son’s school shooting case
item.description: Colin Gray was found guilty of second-degree murder and involuntary manslaughter for giving his son access to a gun and ammunition, which he used to kill two students and two teachers at Apalachee High School in Winder, Georgia.

item.title: Noblesville man arrested, accused of rape of UIndy student in dorm room
item.description: A 21-year-old man was arrested for allegedly raping a University of Indianapolis student in her dorm room after she believed she was drugged at a bar in downtown Indianapolis.

item.title: France moves nuclear-powered aircraft carrier from Baltic Sea to the Mediterranean
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has ordered France's nuclear-powered aircraft carrier to move from the Baltic Sea to the Mediterranean.

item.title: US soldiers who died in Iran war remembered as devoted parents and reservists
item.description: Four U.S. soldiers from the Army Reserve were killed in a drone attack in Kuwait while supporting the military campaign against Iran.

item.title: How 2 Hoosiers are navigating travels to and from the Middle East amid airstrikes
item.description: Two Hoosiers with ties to Dubai are navigating safety concerns and disrupted travel plans due to the Israeli and U.S. strikes on Iran, while the country is quickly working to repair any damage and resume normal business.

item.title: US military launches anti-drug trafficking operation in Ecuador
item.description: The U.S. Southern Command has launched operations against Designated Terrorist Organizations in Ecuador, demonstrating the commitment of partners in Latin America and the Caribbean to combat narco-terrorism.
